approval_gate: Nolan approves every exact post. Silence is not approval.
first_installment_sketch: 'What actually replaces human approval in an autonomous runtime' (directive sec 39, series item 4): walk the replace-it list against one real envelope, e.g. the social engagement passes with per-pass budgets and 60-120s pacing. Concrete runtime-spec citations to be pinned at write time; no invented measurements.
inputs: the invariant list (constitutional invariants, policy, identity, capabilities, budgets, stable intent identity, idempotency, leases, verification, evidence, replay, watchdogs, circuit breakers, bounded adaptation, rollback)
the fail-closed rule for missing authority or verification
name: AUTONOMY AS SAFETY PROPERTY
outputs: one autonomy-as-safety post per envelope or incident
the standing invariant card reused across posts
purpose: Market autonomy as a safety property: ordinary authorized execution needs no per-action approval because the authority envelope is bounded before execution.
template: Never 'PING eliminates humans'. State technically what changed: ORDINARY AUTHORIZED EXECUTION DOES NOT REQUIRE PER-ACTION HUMAN APPROVAL. Then show what replaces it as the full invariant list. Then publish the most important invariant: UNCERTAINTY DOES NOT BECOME PERMISSION. If critical authority or verification disappears: READ MAY CONTINUE WHERE SAFE, NEW EXTERNAL MUTATIONS STOP. Tie each post to a concrete envelope (the social engagement passes run under bounded capabilities, budgets, pacing, durable intent and circuit breakers) and cite the directive's correction note: approval and autonomy are both policies over the same consequential-action substrate.
